I brew more in autumn, as the temperature is stable and at a good level for ales and some lagers. I end up brewing quite a bit of stout and heavier ales to get me through the winter!
How do your brewing habits change by the season?
No doubt about the winter stout season. In spring and summer it is grapefruit ale and other such pale ales. In fall it is nice to have some spiced ales for thanksgiving and Christmas.
Welcome! It is an amazing hobby that you can start at any age/level. You can brew decent beer using items you'll already have in your kitchen :-)

I mainly brew outside. I live in the upper Midwest, so that means that outdoor brewing stops in the winter. I make mead or cider during the colder months.

As for brewing with the seasons, I like to go with wheat beers for the spring/summer. I will start making more fruit flavored beer as the weather gets hotter. For the autumn, I like IPAs/ESBs. I will definitely make a pumpkin beer for October. I tend to have some extra ingredients lying around, so for my last beer, I make a batch where I throw all of the extras in. It changes every year, but it usually is good.
I brew outside so I try to keep with the seasons. I always brew a stout around December and a maibock in January. I usually am brewing ipas all year as they are my favorite.
I look to brew light beers during the summer and darker ones during winter.

I live in Texas and brewing outside during the summer sucks. I can get to a boil a lot more quickly but cooling the wort takes a lot longer. Fall and winter are really the best times for brewing outside here.

For the summer, I prefer light easy-drinking lagers. Cider is also a good summer option for me. I'm about to start a batch of Skeeter Pee.

For the winter, I like making darker spiced beers. Last year I made Juleøl which paired really nice with Thanksgiving foods.
